implementation_notes: The classic per-page controller class collapses into a plain function value: http.HandleFunc("/view/", viewHandler) registers a func(http.ResponseWriter, *http.Request) on a ServeMux, which dispatches by URL pattern, and the handler does request handling, domain calls and template execution in one place, with html/template (or a parsed template set) replacing the view object. Shared behaviour is composed as wrapping middleware (func(http.Handler) http.Handler) instead of inherited from a base controller, and the standard library supplies the whole mapping, so no framework is required. A hand-written controller struct with methods is still reasonable when several pages share state, but the function-per-page form is the idiomatic default.
pitfalls: ServeMux patterns are prefix-based: '/view/' also matches '/view/x/y', so a wrong trailing slash silently changes the page's URL space.
Handlers run concurrently, one goroutine per request: per-page buffers or caches must not be shared through package-level variables without synchronization.
Registering pages on http.DefaultServeMux hides them from tests and from other servers in the same process; build an explicit ServeMux per application.
